messages.author: b8a1da45c9a2eab1
messages.subject: Producing marginal detection function plots
parts:
Hi Folks,

I've fitted some detection functions with covariates using the R package, Distance. I'm using either a half-normal or hazard-rate model with one continuous covariate (e.g. sea state) and potentially one categorical covariate (e.g. precipitation true/false). I'd like to inspect and illustrate the shape of these functions by plotting the predicted detection probability vs. distance for different levels of the covariates. i.e. I'd like to produce marginal detection function plots similar to fig. 7 in Marques, et al. (2007). "Improving estimates of bird density using multiple- covariate distance sampling." The Auk 124(4): 1229-1243. 

Naively, I'd assumed that to do this I could extract the parameter estimates from the ddf object using my.mod$ddf$par, then plug these into equations 5.10, 5.11 and 5.39 in Buckland, et al. (2015) Distance Sampling: Methods and Applications. However, this approach results in nonsense! I suspect that this may be because ds() rescales the explanatory covariates prior to fitting the detection function but without knowing what goes on under the hood in this function it's impossible to know. Can anyone shed any light on how the reported parameter estimates map the expected detection probabilities for half-normal or hazard-rate models? 

By the way, this seems related to several other questions on this list, such as this:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/predict$20ds%7Csort:date/distance-sampling/45KASKev9N4/5Twa5pbUAwAJ

I wonder if some of these questions were prompted by others trying to produce marginal detection function plots as well?

Thanks in advance,

Ewan

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Producing marginal detection function plots
parts:
Ewan

You are correct there is not a general-purpose plotting function for detection functions with covariates.  As you note from your detective work, this subject has come up previously, and the function detfct() has been implicated.

I've knocked together the beginnings of a function to perform what you requested, working only with a single factor covariate.  You could expand on it to produce more elegant plots.  Points to consider along the way:  what values of continuous covariates will you want plotted (the answer is obvious for factor covariates, but not for continuous).  How many combinations of those possible do you wish to have shown?  This issues are why such a full-fledged plotting function hasn't been produced.

Nevertheless, here is a function (it will receive no points for style), but it is reproducible given the data sets in the Distance package.

library(Distance)
conversion.factor <- convert_units("meter", NULL, "hectare")
data(Savannah_sparrow_1980)
Savannah_sparrow_1980.hn.region <- ds(data=Savannah_sparrow_1980, key="hn", truncation=55,
                                      transect="point", convert.units=conversion.factor,
                                      formula=~Region.Label)
plot.with.covariates <- function(dsobject) {
#   Purpose: plot detection function for each level of factor covariate
#   Input:   object of class ds produced by ds()
#   Output:  plot
#   Author:  Rexstad, February 2020
#   Notes:   makes use of function detfct() to do the work.
  myobject <- dsobject$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj
  truncation <- dsobject$ddf$meta.data$width
  mycovariate <- myobject$xmat[,2]  # position in matrix when only a single covariate
  covar.levels <- length(unique(mycovariate))
  dists <- seq(0, truncation)
  xx <- matrix(data=NA, nrow=length(dists), ncol = covar.levels)
  this.dist <- 0
  for (i in dists) {
    this.dist <- this.dist + 1
    xx[this.dist, ] <- unique(detfct(i, myobject))
  }
    plot(dists, xx[,1], type='l', lty=1, ylim=c(0,1),
       xlab="Distance (m)", ylab="Detection probability",
       main="Detection function for levels of factor covariate")
  for (more.levels in 2:covar.levels) {
    lines(dists, xx[,more.levels], type="l", lty=more.levels)
  }
  legend("topright", legend=seq(1:covar.levels),
         lty=seq(1:covar.levels), title="Covariate value")
}
plot.with.covariates(Savannah_sparrow_1980.hn.region)

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Producing marginal detection function plots
parts:
Hi Eric,

Thanks very much for your swift reply and for the suggested approach. As I understand it, detfct() can be used to obtain predictions for some combinations of covariate values/levels but only if these appear in the original data set. Is that correct? Hence, for example, I don't think you can predict detection probabilities at say the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile of the sea state (as in Fig. 9, Campbell, et al. (2015). Deep Sea Res II, 112: 143-157), unless by chance your original data contained detections at these values. 

If that is the case, imagine that there would be some appetite for a function that allowed one predict detection probabilities from a ddf object at specific distances and covariate values/levels. Users could then easily construct their own plots. Do you know if there are any plans to add such a function to Distance or any of the other related packages? Maybe not a trivial ask!

All the best,

Ewan
